name: pricing-card
purpose: One tier of a pricing table: what it is called, what it costs, what that price includes, and the one action that moves the account onto it. The card owns the typographic hierarchy of a price — an overline plan name, the amount as the headline figure, and the billing caveat under it in muted body copy — so a row of tiers reads as a comparison rather than as three differently-typeset cards. `actionsPosition` is the axis that decides which of the two compositions the card is. **`bottom`** is the compact tier: the name, a `medium` amount and the caveat stack at the top, the action follows, and the slot sits under it — a card sized by its own content, for a row of tiers a reader scans. **`middle`** is the full tier: the amount becomes the `large` headline figure, the caveat moves up to `body-md`, the slot grows to fill the card, and the action is pinned to the bottom edge so a row of `middle` cards has its buttons on one line whatever each tier's feature list holds. `variant` decides only whether the card draws its own surface (`contained`) or sits on the one behind it (`ghost`); it never changes the composition. The name, the amount and the caveat are **one column**, capped at `--container-xs` (348px) rather than at the card's full width: the caveat is a sentence about the price directly above it, so it wraps on the price's measure. The cap shipped as `--container-3xs` (256px) — two rungs down the ladder, and too narrow for the copy it holds. 256px sets `body-md` at roughly 33 characters, under the 45–75 a prose measure wants, and all three billing caveats on the sample pricing page (66, 69 and 84 characters) ran to three lines there. At 348px the measure is ~46 characters and the same three set in two, while the card's own content box at 1440 is 413px — so the caveat is still held to the price's column instead of the card's. The card carries **one** prose region — the pricing caveat, below the amount. It used to carry a second paragraph above the amount as well, and with `equalHeight` reserving a band for each, a row of tiers showed two two-line muted blocks around every price doing the same visual job. The Figma component (`3605:2260`) has a single prose region, `Pricing Details`, positioned below the amount, so that is the one the card keeps; a tier's positioning sentence belongs to whatever the consumer puts in the slot. `equalHeight` makes a ROW of cards read as one comparison. Every region is content-sized by default, which is right for a single card and wrong for three side by side — a tier with a two-line caveat and a tier with none put their feature lists on different lines, and the reader has to re-find the row in every column. It reserves **three** lines for the caveat, in `lh` so the reservation follows the type token rather than a hard-coded height. Three is the design's 64px band expressed in whole lines of the region's own token (`body-md` is a 22px line box, so `3lh` is 66px; `2lh` is 44px and twenty short) — it shipped as `2lh`, and the shortfall stayed invisible until a tier's caveat ran to three lines at the region's then-256px measure, overflowed the band, and pushed that column's feature list 22px below the other two. Opt-in, because reserving empty lines is wrong for a lone card; set it on every card in the row. A caveat past three lines still pushes the row down, like any overflow. The plan title is an **overline** (`.text-overline-md` on an `<h3>`): the token carries the display face, the uppercase transform and the widest tracking step, so the tier reads as a label on the card rather than as a title competing with the price beneath it. It stays an `<h3>` for the document outline — the tier is the section heading — while looking like an overline. There is no built-in plan name: set `title` on every card.
useWhen: One tier in a row of plans: plan name, price, billing caveat, one action and the tier's feature list.
A compact tier sized by its content (`actions-position="bottom"`), or a full tier whose action is pinned to the bottom so a row's buttons line up (`actions-position="middle"`).
A tier set on the surface behind it (`variant="ghost"`) inside a section that already draws the frame.
avoidWhen: You need the whole plans band of a pricing page, with the billing-period toggle and the framed row → use `pricing-plans-section`.
You need a feature-by-feature comparison across plans → use `plan-comparison-section`.
You only need to show an amount, in a table cell or a summary → use `currency-amount`.
The card holds general content rather than a price → use `card`.
related: `currency-amount` — typesets the amount inside the card; use it directly for prices outside a tier card.
`pricing-plans-section` — the page section that lays out a row of plan cards with the billing toggle.
`plan-comparison-section` — the matrix that sits under the plan cards.
`card` — generic bordered card with header, content and footer regions.
bestPractices: In a row of tiers, set `equalHeight` on every card so each caveat reserves the same band and the feature lists start on one line.
Keep `pricing-details` to the billing caveat. A tier's positioning sentence goes in the default slot with the feature list.
The card emits no events, and the built-in button has no handler. To act on the click, fill the `actions` slot with your own `Button`.
Hide the symbol or the period with `:show-prefix="false"` / `:show-suffix="false"` (for example on a custom-quote tier) instead of clearing `prefix` / `suffix`.
Mark at most one card in a row with `show-tag` and `tag-label`.

props.name: title
props.doc: Plan name shown as the card heading.

props.name: pricingDetails
props.doc: Caveat under the price, such as the billing terms.

props.name: showTag
props.doc: Shows the tag beside the plan name.

props.name: tagLabel
props.doc: Text of the tag beside the plan name.

props.name: equalHeight
props.doc: Reserves the caveat's band so a row of cards aligns row-for-row. Set it on every card in the row.

props.name: actionsPosition
props.doc: Composition of the card: `bottom` stacks the actions under the price, `middle` puts the price and actions between the header and the default slot.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Whether the card draws its own surface: `contained` has a border and a surface, `ghost` sits on the page.

props.name: value
props.doc: Price amount, already formatted, without the currency symbol.

props.name: prefix
props.doc: Text before the amount, usually the currency symbol.

props.name: suffix
props.doc: Text after the amount, usually the billing period.

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: Label of the default action button.

props.name: animated
props.doc: Fades the old price out and the new one in when the price changes, such as on a billing-period switch.
